title: How wind turbines work
examples: How does the wind actually make electricity?
What part catches the wind force?
Are wind turbines always this big?

explain.say: Today we learn how wind turbines make power for us.
Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: a wind turbine. Look at the blades, the hub and the gearbox. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.
The blades are shaped like wings to catch the moving air.
The blades spin and this turns a big box called the gearbox.
The gearbox makes the spinning very fast for the generator to use.
The generator uses the fast spin to create electricity for us.
These turbines are often built in open fields or offshore on the sea.

draw.text: Built in open fields or offshore.

faq.q: Do wind turbines need a lot of wind to work?
faq.a: Yes, they need a certain amount of wind speed to start turning effectively. Sometimes they need a steady breeze to generate power.
asks: What wind speed is best for turbines?
Can they work with just a little wind?

faq.q: Does the gearbox always change the speed?
faq.a: The gearbox changes the slow spin of the blades into a much faster spin for the generator. This increase in speed is necessary for electricity production.
asks: Why do they need a gearbox?
Does the speed change happen here?

faq.q: Are the blades the only part that catches the wind?
faq.a: No, the blades are the main part that catches the wind's force. They are designed to capture the energy from the moving air.
asks: Which part interacts with the air?

faq.q: How is the electricity sent from the turbine?
faq.a: The electricity generated is sent through cables to a main power grid. This allows the power to reach homes and schools.
asks: Where does the power go after the generator?

faq.q: Are wind turbines always this tall?
faq.a: No, they come in many sizes depending on where they are built. Some smaller ones can power a small community.
asks: What size do they come in?

facts: Wind turbines convert the kinetic energy of wind into mechanical energy.
The blades are designed using principles similar to aircraft wings.
The generator converts the mechanical energy into electrical energy.
Turbines can be built on land or floating in the ocean.

quiz.say: Which part of the turbine catches the initial force from the wind?
quiz.why: The blades are the first part to interact with the moving air.

wrong.0: The gearbox changes the speed, it does not catch the wind.
wrong.1: The tower just holds the parts up high.
wrong.3: The generator uses the spin, it does not catch the wind.

quiz.say: If the blades spin slowly, what component increases that speed?
quiz.why: The gearbox is specifically designed to increase the rotational speed.

wrong.1: The blades only catch the wind's energy.
wrong.2: The generator needs the speed to work, it does not create it.
wrong.3: The tower is just a support structure.

quiz.say: The process of making electricity from wind involves which sequence?
quiz.why: This order shows the energy transfer from wind to electricity.

wrong.0: The generator needs the spin from the gearbox.
wrong.1: The gearbox must speed up the spin before the generator.
wrong.3: The gearbox needs the blades to spin first.
